books.section: Topic 4.12 African Americans in the Early Republic, B. The Cultures of African-American Communities

stimulus.text:
Free Black men organized to defend their rights. In September 1830, delegates from several Northern states met at Mother Bethel Church in Philadelphia, chose Richard Allen as president, and formed a society to improve the condition of free people of color and plan a settlement in Canada.

At the same time, Northern states were narrowing Black men’s rights: New York’s 1821 constitution dropped the property test for white voters but kept a $250 property requirement for Black voters, and Pennsylvania’s 1838 constitution limited the vote to white men. New York had ended slavery only gradually, with final emancipation in 1827.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the first National Negro Convention, September 1830, from John W. Cromwell, The Early Negro Convention Movement, and of the voting restrictions in the New York constitution of 1821 and the Pennsylvania constitution of 1838.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from Cromwell, The Early Negro Convention Movement
stem: The voting rules described in the passage best show what about the expansion of democracy in the 1820s and 1830s?

options.text: It expanded for white men while narrowing for Black men
It gave Black men the vote on the same terms as white men
options.misconception: A $250 requirement applied to Black men only, and Pennsylvania barred them.

options.text: It ended property tests for all voters by 1838
options.misconception: The $250 test stayed for Black voters in New York.

options.text: It left voting rules unchanged from the founding era
options.misconception: New York dropped the test for whites and kept one for Blacks; Pennsylvania changed its constitution.

rationales.A: New York dropped the property test for white men but kept a $250 one for Black men, and Pennsylvania barred Black men outright.
rationales.B: The terms were not the same. Black men in New York needed $250 in property; white men did not.
rationales.C: Property tests did not end for everyone. The $250 requirement for Black voters in New York stayed in place.
rationales.D: The rules changed. New York rewrote its constitution in 1821 and Pennsylvania rewrote its own in 1838.
rationales.general:
1. Compare the two rules in New York. White men lost the property test; Black men kept a $250 one.
2. Add Pennsylvania. Its 1838 constitution limited the vote to white men.
3. Name the pattern. Democracy widened for one group and narrowed for another.
Background: By 1860, free Black men could vote on equal terms in only five New England states.
Remember: ask who gains and who loses before calling an age democratic.
